questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the fiscal deficit in Union Budget 2026-27:
1. The fiscal deficit for 2026-27 (BE) is placed at 4.3 per cent of GDP.
2. The Revised Estimate for 2025-26 is 4.8 per cent of GDP.
3. The Budget describes the commitment to bring the fiscal deficit below 4.5 per cent of GDP by 2025-26 as fulfilled.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Revised Estimate for 2025-26 is 4.4 per cent, which is why the 4.5 per cent commitment counts as met; 4.8 per cent was the 2024-25 level. The 2026-27 BE is a further step down to 4.3 per cent.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A)

questions.q:
Statement-I: Union Budget 2026-27 estimates the Centre's debt-to-GDP ratio at 55.6 per cent in BE 2026-27, down from 56.1 per cent in RE 2025-26.
Statement-II: The Budget retains the goal of bringing the debt-to-GDP ratio to 50 plus or minus 1 per cent by 2030-31.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are in the Budget speech. The medium-term goal is a destination set earlier; it does not explain why the ratio dips by 0.5 percentage point this year, so Statement-II is a separate fact.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A)
questions.h: Debt path: 56.1 to 55.6, aim 50 plus-minus 1 by 2031

questions.q:
Statement-I: A fiscal deficit of 4.3 per cent of GDP in Union Budget 2026-27 means the Centre's total expenditure exceeds its total non-debt receipts by that margin.
Statement-II: The fiscal deficit equals the Government's total borrowing requirement for the year.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Fiscal deficit is total expenditure minus revenue receipts and non-debt capital receipts. Whatever expenditure is not met from non-debt receipts must be financed by borrowing, so Statement-II explains Statement-I.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Fiscal Policy); Union Budget 2026-27

questions.q: In Union Budget 2026-27, gross borrowing through dated securities is Rs 17.2 lakh crore, while net borrowing through dated securities is Rs 11.7 lakh crore. The gap of about Rs 5.5 lakh crore mainly represents:
o: redemption of earlier dated securities falling due
Ways and Means Advances from the RBI
questions.e: Net borrowing is gross borrowing minus repayments of previously issued securities. Heavier maturities from past years raise the gross figure without adding to the new debt the Centre takes on.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A); Budget at a Glance

questions.q:
Consider the following figures from Union Budget 2026-27:
1. Total expenditure (BE 2026-27) of Rs 53.5 lakh crore.
2. Non-debt receipts (BE 2026-27) of Rs 36.5 lakh crore.
3. Net tax receipts (BE 2026-27) of Rs 26.7 lakh crore.
4. Total expenditure (RE 2025-26) of Rs 49.6 lakh crore.
How many of the above are correct?
questions.e: Rs 26.7 lakh crore is the net tax receipts figure for RE 2025-26; BE 2026-27 net tax receipts are Rs 28.7 lakh crore. The other three figures are as in the Budget speech.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A)

questions.q: The Union Budget 2026-27 proposes public capital expenditure of Rs 12.2 lakh crore, compared with Rs 2 lakh crore in 2014-15. The 2026-27 outlay is approximately how many times the 2014-15 level?
questions.e: 12.2 divided by 2 is about 6.1. The Budget also notes Rs 11.2 lakh crore in BE 2025-26, so the increase for 2026-27 is a further push on an already high base.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 16th Finance Commission and Union Budget 2026-27:
1. The Commission was chaired by Arvind Panagariya.
2. The Commission recommended raising the States' vertical share of the divisible pool from 41 per cent to 42 per cent.
3. The Budget provides Rs 1.4 lakh crore to States for 2026-27 as Finance Commission grants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The vertical devolution share remains at 41 per cent; 42 per cent was the 14th Finance Commission's figure. The grants for 2026-27 include rural and urban local body grants and disaster management grants.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A); Article 280

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Finance Commission of India is NOT correct?
o: Article 280 provides for the President to constitute it at the expiration of every fifth year or earlier.
Its recommendations are laid before Parliament along with an explanatory memorandum on action taken.
It recommends how the net proceeds of Union taxes are to be shared between the Union and the States.
Its recommendations are binding on the Union Government.
questions.e: Finance Commission recommendations are advisory; the Government need not accept them, though it lays the report and an action-taken memorandum before Parliament under Article 281. That is why the 41 per cent share in the 16th FC's report is a policy choice the Centre accepted.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch (Finance Commission); Articles 280-281

questions.q:
Match List-I (Article of the Constitution) with List-II (Subject):
List-I
A. Article 112
B. Article 114
C. Article 115
D. Article 116
List-II
1. Supplementary, additional or excess grants
2. Vote on account
3. Annual financial statement
4. Appropriation Bills
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Budget is presented under Article 112, the Appropriation Bill authorises spending under Article 114, supplementary grants fall under Article 115, and votes on account under Article 116.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 'Parliament' (Financial Legislation); Articles 112-116
questions.h: 112 statement, 113 demands, 114 appropriation, 115 supplementary, 116 vote on account

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Contingency Fund of India:
1. It is established under Article 267 of the Constitution.
2. Each advance from it requires the prior approval of Parliament.
3. It is held by the Finance Secretary on behalf of the President.
4. It is created under the Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The fund is in the nature of an imprest: the Executive can draw on it for urgent unforeseen expenditure and seek Parliament's approval afterwards, then recoup it. Prior approval is therefore not required, which is the trap in statement 2.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 'Parliament'; Article 267

questions.q: Which one of the following expenditures is NOT charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
o: Salary of the Comptroller and Auditor General
Salary of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: Charged expenditure, listed in Article 112(3), is discussed but not voted on. It covers the President, the Speaker, judges of the Supreme Court, the CAG and debt charges, while ministers' salaries are voted.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 'Parliament'; Article 112(3)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) in Union Budget 2026-27:
1. The MAT rate is reduced from 15 per cent to 14 per cent.
2. From 1 April 2026, MAT becomes a final tax with no further credit accumulation.
3. Brought-forward MAT credit can be set off without any limit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Set-off of earlier credit is allowed only under the new regime and capped at one-fourth of tax liability, so statement 3 fails. Making MAT final at 14 per cent removes the credit build-up.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part B); PIB Summary of Union Budget 2026-27

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Securities Transaction Tax (STT) changes in Union Budget 2026-27:
1. STT on futures is raised from 0.02 per cent to 0.05 per cent.
2. STT on options premium is raised from 0.1 per cent to 0.15 per cent.
3. STT on options exercise is raised from 0.125 per cent to 0.20 per cent.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Options exercise STT goes from 0.125 per cent to 0.15 per cent, not 0.20 per cent. The Budget raised STT on all three derivative legs, but by different amounts.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part B); PIB Summary of Union Budget 2026-27
questions.h: Futures x2.5; premium and exercise both land on 0.15

questions.q: Under Union Budget 2026-27, buyback of shares is taxed as capital gains for all shareholders, with an additional tax on promoters. The effective tax rates on buybacks for corporate promoters and non-corporate promoters are, respectively:
questions.e: The promoter surcharge in the form of additional buyback tax lifts the effective rate to 22 per cent for corporate promoters and 30 per cent for non-corporate promoters.
questions.s: PIB Summary of Union Budget 2026-27, 1 Feb 2026

questions.q: Which one of the following changes in Tax Collected at Source (TCS) was announced in Union Budget 2026-27?
o: TCS on sale of scrap and minerals abolished
TCS on overseas tour packages fixed at 20 per cent for all amounts
TCS on tendu leaves raised from 2 per cent to 5 per cent
TCS on LRS remittances for education and medical purposes reduced from 5 per cent to 2 per cent
questions.e: The Budget rationalises TCS to 2 per cent for overseas tour packages (earlier 5 or 20 per cent), for LRS remittances for education and medical purposes (earlier 5 per cent) and for tendu leaves (earlier 5 per cent). Liquor, scrap and minerals move from 1 to 2 per cent.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part B)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about customs measures in Union Budget 2026-27:
1. The tariff on dutiable goods imported for personal use is cut from 20 per cent to 10 per cent.
2. The Rs 10 lakh per-consignment cap on courier exports is removed.
3. Duty deferral for eligible Authorised Economic Operators is extended from 15 days to 30 days.
4. The validity of advance rulings is reduced from 5 years to 3 years.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Advance ruling validity is extended from 3 years to 5 years, not reduced. The other three measures come from the Budget's trust-based customs and ease-of-living package.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part B); PIB Summary of Union Budget 2026-27

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the direct tax proposals in Union Budget 2026-27?
o: The Income-tax Act, 2025 comes into effect from April 2026.
The deadline for filing revised returns is extended from 31 December to 31 March.
New individual slab rates with a higher basic exemption limit are introduced.
A one-time six-month foreign asset disclosure scheme is offered to small taxpayers.
questions.e: The Budget speech contains no change in individual tax slabs; its direct tax proposals focus on ease of living, dispute resolution and corporate provisions. The other three options are among its stated measures.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part B); PIB Summary of Union Budget 2026-27

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about IT services in Union Budget 2026-27:
1. Software development, IT-enabled services, KPO and contract R&D are grouped into one IT Services category.
2. A common safe harbour margin of 15.5 per cent applies to the category.
3. The safe harbour threshold is raised from Rs 100 crore to Rs 1,000 crore.
4. Foreign cloud service providers using Indian data centres get a tax holiday up to 2047.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The threshold rises from Rs 300 crore to Rs 2,000 crore, so statement 3 uses the wrong figures. A single category with a 15.5 per cent margin and a tax holiday to 2047 are as in the Budget.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part B); PIB Summary of Union Budget 2026-27

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Money Bills:
1. A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha.
2. The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within 14 days of receipt.
3. The Rajya Sabha can amend a Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes to a Money Bill, and the Lok Sabha is free to accept or reject them, so statement 3 is wrong. This is why the Appropriation Bill and Finance Bill from the Budget pass through the Lok Sabha's will.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 'Parliament'; Articles 109-110

questions.q:
Match the type of cut motion (List-I) with its effect (List-II):
List-I
A. Policy cut
B. Economy cut
C. Token cut
List-II
1. Demand reduced by Rs 100
2. Demand reduced to Re 1
3. Demand reduced by a specified amount
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: A policy cut signals disapproval of policy by cutting the demand to Re 1, an economy cut reduces it by a specified amount to push economy, and a token cut of Rs 100 airs a specific grievance.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 'Parliament'; Budget procedure
questions.h: Policy: Re 1; Economy: specified; Token: Rs 100

questions.q: In a given year, a government has a fiscal deficit of Rs 16,000 crore, interest payments of Rs 9,000 crore, a revenue deficit of Rs 8,000 crore and grants for creation of capital assets of Rs 3,000 crore. Its primary deficit and effective revenue deficit are, respectively:
questions.e: Primary deficit is the fiscal deficit minus interest payments (16,000 - 9,000 = 7,000). Effective revenue deficit is the revenue deficit minus grants for creating capital assets (8,000 - 3,000 = 5,000).
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Fiscal Policy)

questions.q:
Statement-I: In Union Budget 2026-27, the Centre's net tax receipts of Rs 28.7 lakh crore are lower than its gross tax revenue.
Statement-II: A part of the Centre's gross tax revenue is devolved to the States, and net tax receipts are what remain after that.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Gross tax revenue is split between the Centre and States according to the Finance Commission's formula (41 per cent vertical share). Net tax receipts are what stays with the Centre, so the transfer to States explains why net is lower than gross.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A); Article 270

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Union Budget 2026-27:
1. It was presented on 1 February 2026 as the ninth consecutive Budget of Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.
2. It was organised around three 'kartavyas'.
3. It was the first Union Budget after the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Railway Budget was merged with the General Budget from 2017-18, so 2026-27 was not the first after the merger. The 2026-27 Budget's three kartavyas cover growth, aspirations and capacity, and inclusion.
questions.s: ETV Bharat, 1 Feb 2026; PIB, 1 Feb 2026

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law?
questions.e: Article 265 is the constitutional bar on taxation without legislative backing. Article 266 deals with the Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts, and Articles 268 and 270 deal with distribution of tax proceeds.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 'Parliament' / Constitutional provisions; Article 265

questions.q:
Statement-I: Expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India cannot be incurred without Parliament's authorisation.
Statement-II: Article 266(3) provides that no money out of the Consolidated Fund shall be appropriated except in accordance with law and for the purposes and in the manner provided in the Constitution.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 266(3) is the constitutional basis of the rule: spending from the Consolidated Fund needs an Appropriation Act. That is why the Appropriation Bill is part of every Budget cycle.
questions.s: Laxmikanth Ch 'Parliament'; Article 266

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Biopharma SHAKTI announced in Union Budget 2026-27:
1. It has an outlay of Rs 10,000 crore over five years.
2. It includes five new NIPERs and the upgrade of three existing NIPERs.
3. It aims at a network of over 1,000 accredited clinical trial sites.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Budget provides for three new NIPERs and upgrades to seven existing ones; the numbers in statement 2 are wrong. The outlay and the clinical trial network are as announced.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026; PIB, 1 Feb 2026

questions.q: Under Union Budget 2026-27, the outlay of the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (launched in April 2025) is proposed to be raised from Rs 22,919 crore to:
questions.e: The Budget raises the scheme's outlay to Rs 40,000 crore as part of its push on seven strategic and frontier sectors. The sectors also include semiconductors (ISM 2.0), rare earths and biopharma.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A); PIB Summary of Union Budget 2026-27

questions.q: Union Budget 2026-27 announces Rare Earth Corridors for mineral-rich States. Which one of the following States is NOT among those named?
questions.e: The Budget names Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu for the corridors. The Budget also cuts customs duty on monazite from 2.5 per cent to nil.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A and B)

questions.q: Union Budget 2026-27 proposes seven high-speed rail corridors as 'growth connectors'. Which one of the following is NOT among them?
questions.e: The seven corridors are Mumbai-Pune, Pune-Hyderabad, Hyderabad-Bengaluru, Hyderabad-Chennai, Chennai-Bengaluru, Delhi-Varanasi and Varanasi-Siliguri. Delhi-Amritsar is not in the list.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about City Economic Regions (CERs) in Union Budget 2026-27:
1. Rs 5,000 crore over five years is proposed for each CER.
2. Financing follows a reform-cum-results model.
3. Rs 5,000 crore is the combined outlay for all CERs together.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Budget gives Rs 5,000 crore per CER over five years, linked to reforms and results. It is not a total for all regions, which is the trap in statement 3.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A); PIB Summary of Union Budget 2026-27
questions.h: Rs 5,000 crore each, not in total

questions.q: Union Budget 2026-27 announced a scheme for Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS) with an outlay of:
questions.e: The Budget sets aside Rs 20,000 crore over five years for CCUS, aimed at hard-to-abate sectors such as power, steel, cement, refineries and chemicals, under its energy security theme.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A)

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II as per Union Budget 2026-27:
List-I
A. SME Growth Fund
B. Additional infusion into the Self-Reliant India Fund
C. Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage scheme (five years)
D. Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (revised outlay)
List-II (Rs crore)
1. 2,000
2. 10,000
3. 20,000
4. 40,000
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The SME Growth Fund is Rs 10,000 crore to nurture 'champion' MSMEs, with Rs 2,000 crore more for the Self-Reliant India Fund; CCUS is Rs 20,000 crore and the revised ECMS outlay Rs 40,000 crore.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A)

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II as per Union Budget 2026-27:
List-I
A. Chemical parks proposed through the challenge route
B. Hi-Tech Tool Rooms to be set up by CPSEs (locations)
C. Legacy industrial clusters to be revived
D. Container Manufacturing Scheme (over Rs ... crore across five years)
List-II
1. 2
2. 3
3. 200
4. 10,000
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Budget announces three chemical parks, Hi-Tech Tool Rooms at two locations, revival of 200 legacy industrial clusters and a Container Manufacturing Scheme of over Rs 10,000 crore across five years.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A)

questions.q: Which one of the following statements regarding transport announcements in Union Budget 2026-27 is NOT correct?
o: A dedicated freight corridor from Dankuni in the East to Surat in the West is planned.
Twenty new National Waterways are to be developed over five years, starting with NW-5 in Odisha.
A Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme aims to raise the share of inland waterways and coastal shipping in cargo from 6 per cent to 12 per cent by 2047.
A new dedicated freight corridor from Ludhiana to Mumbai is announced.
questions.e: The Budget announces a freight corridor from Dankuni (West Bengal) to Surat (Gujarat). No Ludhiana-Mumbai corridor is announced.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A)
questions.h: Dankuni to Surat; waterways 6 to 12 by 2047

questions.q:
Match the textile initiative (List-I) with its focus (List-II) as per Union Budget 2026-27:
List-I
A. National Fibre Scheme
B. Textile Expansion and Employment Scheme
C. Mahatma Gandhi Gram Swaraj initiative
D. Mega Textile Parks (challenge mode)
List-II
1. Traditional clusters
2. Natural, man-made and new-age fibres
3. Khadi, handloom and handicrafts
4. Technical textiles
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: These sit under the Budget's integrated textile programme: the National Fibre Scheme covers fibres, the Expansion and Employment Scheme covers traditional clusters, the Gram Swaraj initiative supports khadi, handloom and handicrafts, and the mega parks focus on technical textiles.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A); ETV Bharat, 1 Feb 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about health-related announcements in Union Budget 2026-27:
1. 100,000 Allied Health Professionals are to be added over five years.
2. Five Regional Medical Hubs are to be set up with States and private partners.
3. Three new All India Institutes of Ayurveda are to be established.
4. Ten new AIIMS are to be established in the Purvodaya States.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are in the Budget. No set of ten new AIIMS for Purvodaya States was announced.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A); PIB, 1 Feb 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about animal husbandry in Union Budget 2026-27:
1. A loan-linked capital subsidy is offered for private veterinary and para-veterinary colleges, hospitals, labs and breeding facilities.
2. The aim is to add more than 20,000 veterinary professionals.
3. The aim is to add over 2 lakh veterinary professionals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Budget targets over 20,000 additional veterinary professionals, not 2 lakh, so statements 2 and 3 cannot both hold. The capital subsidy is loan-linked.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A); PIB Summary of Union Budget 2026-27

questions.q: AVGC Content Creator Labs announced in Union Budget 2026-27 are to be set up in how many secondary schools and colleges?
questions.e: AVGC stands for animation, visual effects, gaming and comics. The labs, anchored with IICT Mumbai, target 15,000 secondary schools and 500 colleges for the orange economy.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A); ETV Bharat, 1 Feb 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about education and tourism announcements in Union Budget 2026-27:
1. Five University Townships are to be developed near industrial and logistics corridors.
2. One girls' hostel is to be provided in every block of the country.
3. The National Council for Hotel Management is to be upgraded to a National Institute of Hospitality.
4. A new National Institute of Design is to be set up in western India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are in the Budget. The hostel is one per district, and the new National Institute of Design is for eastern India.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A); PIB Summary of Union Budget 2026-27

questions.q:
Union Budget 2026-27 proposes developing 15 archaeological sites as tourist destinations. Match the site (List-I) with its State (List-II):
List-I
A. Lothal
B. Rakhigarhi
C. Adichanallur
D. Hastinapur
List-II
1. Haryana
2. Uttar Pradesh
3. Tamil Nadu
4. Gujarat
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Lothal is a Harappan port town in Gujarat, Rakhigarhi a major Harappan site in Haryana, Adichanallur an urn-burial site in Tamil Nadu, and Hastinapur the Mahabharata-linked site in Uttar Pradesh. All four are named in the Budget.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026; Nitin Singhania / NCERT (Indus Valley sites)

questions.q: The Union Budget 2026-27 announces a pilot to upskill 10,000 tourist guides. At how many sites is this pilot proposed?
questions.e: The pilot covers 10,000 guides at 20 sites, with a 12-week course. It goes with digital heritage documentation and a National Destination Digital Knowledge Grid.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A)

questions.q: Bharat-VISTAAR, announced in Union Budget 2026-27, is:
o: a multilingual AI tool linking AgriStack portals with ICAR packages of practices
a crop insurance portal run by the Ministry of Finance
a digital land records system for rural property
a fertiliser subsidy direct benefit transfer system
questions.e: Bharat-VISTAAR is an AI-based advisory tool for farmers in multiple languages that connects the AgriStack portals with ICAR practices. The other options describe unrelated initiatives.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A)

questions.q: Under Union Budget 2026-27, which two National Mental Health Institutes are to be upgraded to Regional Apex Institutions?
questions.e: The Budget upgrades the National Mental Health Institutes at Ranchi and Tezpur to Regional Apex Institutions and proposes NIMHANS-2 in north India.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A); PIB, 1 Feb 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Purvodaya and North-East announcements in Union Budget 2026-27:
1. An integrated East Coast Industrial Corridor is planned with a node at Durgapur.
2. 4,000 e-buses are announced for the Purvodaya States.
3. A Buddhist Circuits scheme is announced for Bihar, Jharkhand and Odisha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Buddhist Circuits scheme is for Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Assam, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura, not Bihar, Jharkhand and Odisha. The other two items are in the Budget.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A); PIB Summary of Union Budget 2026-27

questions.q: Union Budget 2026-27 offers an incentive of Rs 100 crore for a single municipal bond issuance exceeding:
questions.e: The Budget encourages municipal borrowing by giving Rs 100 crore as incentive for a single issuance above Rs 1,000 crore, alongside AMRUT support for smaller issues.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about infrastructure financing announcements in Union Budget 2026-27:
1. An Infrastructure Risk Guarantee Fund offering partial credit guarantees is to be set up.
2. Dedicated REITs are to monetise real estate assets of CPSEs.
3. Hi-Tech Tool Rooms are to be set up at five locations by private firms.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Hi-Tech Tool Rooms are planned at two locations and run by CPSEs, not five by private firms. The risk guarantee fund and CPSE REITs are as announced.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A); The Week, 1 Feb 2026

questions.q: What are 'SHE-Marts' referred to in Union Budget 2026-27?
o: Community-owned retail outlets for rural women's enterprises
Stock market literacy centres for women investors
Digital payment kiosks run by banks
questions.e: SHE-Marts (Self-Help Entrepreneur Marts) are community-owned retail outlets that give rural women's enterprises a market. They are part of the Budget's inclusion-focused kartavya.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A)

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the focus areas of India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 announced in Union Budget 2026-27?
o: Equipment and materials for semiconductor manufacturing
Subsidies for imports of finished smartphones
questions.e: ISM 2.0 targets equipment and materials, Indian full-stack IP design, supply-chain resilience and industry-led research and training centres. Import subsidies for finished phones are not part of it.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A); The Week, 1 Feb 2026

questions.q: Union Budget 2026-27 proposes 'Corporate Mitras' in Tier-II and Tier-III towns. Which professional bodies are asked to design short modular courses for them?
questions.e: The Chartered Accountants, Company Secretaries and Cost and Management Accountants institutes are to build modular courses so para-professionals can help small companies with compliance.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about agriculture and fisheries announcements in Union Budget 2026-27:
1. Integrated development of 500 reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars is proposed.
2. A Coconut Promotion Scheme is announced.
3. Support is announced for tea, coffee and rubber cultivation in coastal areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Budget supports coconut, sandalwood, cocoa and cashew in coastal areas, not tea, coffee and rubber. The 500-reservoir fisheries programme and the Coconut Promotion Scheme are both announced.
questions.s: Budget Speech 2026-27, PIB, 1 Feb 2026 (Part A); PIB, 1 Feb 2026
